text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool `veridian-prod-pool` is at 96% GPU allocation. Queue depth: 312. Active allocations: 48. Top consumer: tenant `veridian-health` (~92% of pooled GPUs). Potential latency SLO breach within 6 mins if trend continues. Auto-scaler failing to provision (quota or region hot). Paging on-call.

alyssa_sre: Acked. Looking now. Can someone share the allocator logs and autoscaler errors? If autoscaler can't get nodes, we need a manual burst or traffic shaping.

marc_mlinfra: Pasted recent scheduler errors from control plane:
```
2025-11-09T14:01:12Z alloc-controller ERROR: quota exhausted in eu-west-1, request 4 gpus denied
2025-11-09T14:03:08Z pool-manager WARN: tenant veridian-health pinned fraction 0.92, preemptible 0
2025-11-09T14:05:41Z runtime INFO: queue length spike: 312, avg wait 4.2s -> 8.9s
```
Looks like cloud quota in region and the pool has heavy single-tenant skew. Autoscaler is healthy but cloud can't allocate.

jess_cs: @alyssa_sre @sam_sales Jess from CS here. Customer impact: VeridianHealth is hitting interactive chat endpoints (mission-critical clinical triage). They called Ops earlier about slow responses. We need to confirm mitigation before SLA hit. Sam — are we allowed to burst on their contract?

sam_sales: Sam here. Verified with account: emergency burst is allowed for 1 hour (overage billed at premium). They want availability > quality. Give me a heads up before we enable anything that affects billing.

alyssa_sre: Ok. Proposed immediate mitigations (ordered):
1) Enable emergency burst +2 GPUs to this pool for 60m (manual).
2) Apply tenant-level QPS throttle for background/bulk jobs (reduce by 40%) to free GPUs.
3) Route new requests from VeridianHealth to a smaller quantized model as fallback for non-critical routes (`vh-fallback:vllm-7b-q4`) for 30-60m.
4) Evict any queued low-priority batch allocations in `veridian-prod-pool`.
I can do 1 & 4 if we have go-ahead from sales. Who will own 2 & 3?

marc_mlinfra: I can own 3 (routing override). Tradeoffs: vllm-7b-q4 reduces GPU memory and latency but reduces generation quality for some prompts. Recommend only for non-clinical-high-risk endpoints (we have routing tags for that). Command to set route:```
rictl routing override set --tenant veridian-health --route /chat/background --model vllm-7b-q4 --duration 60m --reason "emergency pool saturation"
```
Will also enable aggressive prefix caching for that tenant to reduce token work:```
rictl cache policy apply --tenant veridian-health --policy aggressive-prefix --ttl 30m
```

ryan_oncall: I'm prepping manual burst. Need confirmation from Sam for billing and Jess for customer impact. Sam? Jess?

sam_sales: Confirmed. VeridianHealth approves emergency burst for 60 minutes. They asked to be notified when we start and when we stop.

jess_cs: Confirmed. I'll notify the customer with a short note before we flip anything and after. Keep the fallback for background only. Clinical endpoints must remain on primary model if possible.

alyssa_sre: Executing step 1 & 4 now. Running manual burst command:```
rictl pools burst --pool veridian-prod-pool --gpus +2 --duration 60m --reason "tenant saturation: veridian-health emergency"
```
Output: ```
STARTING BURST: pool veridian-prod-pool; +2 GPUs; duration 60m
Allocating nodes in eu-west-1... request submitted (req-0a7c).
```
Waiting for nodes to register.

devops-bot: BURST JOB UPDATE: req-0a7c -> nodes registered (2 GPU nodes) at 2025-11-09T14:12:08Z. Pool allocation updated: 50 -> 52 GPUs.

alyssa_sre: Burst up. Pool allocation now 52 GPUs. Queue depth down from 312 -> 86 over last 2m. Latency trending down.

marc_mlinfra: I'm applying routing override for background chat now. Running:```
rictl routing override set --tenant veridian-health --route /chat/background --model vllm-7b-q4 --duration 60m
```
Applied. Verify: `rictl routing override list --tenant veridian-health` shows background route -> vllm-7b-q4.

nate_engruntime: Also toggled aggressive KV cache for prefixes for that tenant. Expect token reduction ~18-25% after warmup.

alyssa_sre: Good. Now evicting low-priority batch jobs from pool:```
rictl allocations evict --pool veridian-prod-pool --priority batch --dry-run=false --reason "free capacity for interactive"
```
Evicted 6 allocations, freed ~1.5 GPUs.

ryan_oncall: Applying tenant-level throttle for background endpoints (40% reduction). Command:```
rictl quota set --tenant veridian-health --route /chat/background --qps-multiplier 0.6 --duration 60m --reason "emergency throttle to protect SLOs"
```
Applied. Monitoring metrics.

incident-bot: Incident note: manual burst + routing override + throttles applied. Current pool GPUs: 52. Queue: 42. Average latency (p95): 420ms -> target <500ms. No immediate errors.

tanya_prod: Quick product note — need to document how fallback model changed hallucination risk for background prompts. Postmortem should include evals on common prompt sets. I'll open a follow-up ticket.

sam_sales: Notifying billing: emergency overage will be recorded under account VERIDIAN-001. Sam will send confirmation to customer.

jess_cs: Notifying customer now (short message and expected duration).

alyssa_sre: I'll keep monitoring for 30m. If queue stabilizes <60 and p95 <500ms we can consider reducing burst to +1 or letting it expire. If trend reverses, we'll escalate to region ops for quota request or consider cross-region spillover.

ryan_oncall: Handoff: I'm taking the watch for next 2 hours. Alyssa handing off. Alyssa — any outstanding TODOs?

alyssa_sre: Nothing immediate. TODOs:
- @marc_mlinfra validate fallback quality telemetry and revert if harmful.
- @nate_engruntime verify cache warmup impact and evictions.
- @sam_sales finalize billing note and customer confirmation.
- @tanya_prod open PM ticket for evaluation and docs.
I sign off to @ryan_oncall.

ryan_oncall: Ack. Monitoring dashboards linked: https://console.redwood/in/ops/pools/veridian-prod-pool, alerting set to degrade to P1 if p95 > 750ms.

incident-bot: NOTE: last_message_ts=1739206245. Incident state: mitigated (P0->P1). Please follow the runbook for post-incident review.

ryan_oncall: Closing loop — after 40m burst we observed sustained improvement. Queue down to 18, p95 ~380ms. Will let burst expire in ~15m and monitor. If everything stays green, I'll create a brief postmortem and assign owners per Alyssa's TODO list.

jess_cs: Customer updated: they acknowledged the temporary reduction on background routes and accepted the overage. Will coordinate post-incident call tomorrow.

marc_mlinfra: I'll run quick roll-forward tests against vllm-7b-q4 and collect quality diffs vs primary models for tonight's PM ticket.

nate_engruntime: Keeping cache policy for 60m then reverting to normal.

ryan_oncall: End of thread — monitoring continued in the incident channel, POCs assigned.
